title: Value iteration and its error bound
brief: Apply the Bellman optimality backup over and over, watch the error shrink by a factor of gamma per sweep, and compute how many sweeps a target accuracy needs.
hints: One sweep is new = rlenvs.q_from_v(mdp, v).max(axis=1). Compute the whole new vector from the old one before you replace it.
value_iteration's history starts with V_0 and gains one row per sweep, including the last one, so np.array(history) has shape (sweeps + 1, S).
sweeps_needed solves gamma^k * initial_error <= eps for k: math.ceil(math.log(eps / initial_error) / math.log(gamma)). Return 0 when the initial error is already small enough.
